name: Sheko
catalog_citation: Hellenthal, Anne-Christie. 2010. A grammar of Sheko. PhD dissertation, Leiden University. LOT Dissertation Series 258. Utrecht: LOT.
catalog_locator: Chapter 4 'Tone', pp. 111-114 (chapter opening and 4.1 Overview) and 4.7 'Distribution of tone', p. 127 (printed page numbers)
catalog_quote: This chapter gives an overview of tone in Sheko, including its functions, its realisation, and its distribution. Sheko has four level tonemes. These play a role in the lexicon and in the grammar. The levels are numbered from 1 (lowest) to 4 (highest). ... Tone in Sheko has a lexical as well as a grammatical functional load. Tone can be characterized as follows: On the whole, tone in Sheko appears as stable. There is no downstep (not to be expected with four levels of height). One of the major functions of tone is to distinguish between persons. This distinction is found with pronouns, possessor prefixes and verbal subject clitics. ... All verbs can be classified H or L. Tone on verb stems in the TAM paradigms is predictable once the lexical tone class is known. The two classes cover the range of four levels of tone in inflection. ... audit.action: cite a better source for the same coding
audit.reasoning: The classification 'tonal' rests on the standard and only reference grammar of Sheko (Hellenthal 2010, 517 pp.), held as the publisher's open-access PDF; the deciding quotation is verbatim at the stated pages (confirmed in the decoded text and on the rendered image of printed p.111; the second reader had also checked pp.113/127 images). The grammar describes four level tonemes with lexical and grammatical load and contains no stress/accent statement (grep confirms). Older phonologies (Aklilu 1988, 1996) differ only in positing three tones, per the grammar's own review (p.112). Nothing in the Glottolog bibliography is a better or contrary source; the 2023 handbook sketch is by the same author. Only improvement: the evidence grade 'publisher-text' is conservative given page-image verification — could be raised to page-image-backed. No recode.
